questions.stem: India's fiscal deficit for April-September FY27 has widened to 42.1% of the full-year target. In this context, consider the following statements regarding fiscal deficit and related concepts under India's fiscal framework:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Fiscal deficit refers to the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings.
The FRBM Act, 2003 fixes the fiscal deficit target at 3% of GDP for the Union Government with no provision for deviation under any circumstances.
Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
Effective revenue deficit excludes grants given for creation of capital assets from the revenue deficit.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 correctly define fiscal deficit, revenue deficit and effective revenue deficit respectively. Statement 2 is wrong because the FRBM Act contains an 'escape clause' (Section 4(2)) permitting deviation from the target during national security, calamity or severe economic stress.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's fiscal deficit for April-September at Rs 7.14 lakh crore, widens to 42.1% of FY27 aim
questions.pyqLink: Tests FRBM Act provisions and deficit definitions; similar to UPSC 2015/2016 prelims questions distinguishing fiscal, revenue, primary and effective revenue deficit.

questions.stem: A World Bank report shows India's extreme poverty rate falling sharply between 2011 and 2023. In this context, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is jointly published by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
The World Bank's lower-middle-income poverty line is currently set at $2.15 per day at 2017 purchasing power parity (PPP).
Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) exchange rates adjust for differences in price levels across countries so that a common basket of goods costs the same in international dollars.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong as India's National MPI is released by NITI Aayog, not MoSPI. Statement 3 is wrong because, per the article, the World Bank now uses $4.20/day at 2021 PPP as the lower-middle-income poverty line, not the older $2.15/2017 PPP figure.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Extreme poverty in India falls to 2.6% from 27.1%: World Bank
questions.pyqLink: Tests poverty-line definitions and MPI institutional ownership; similar to UPSC prelims questions on NITI Aayog's National MPI (asked around 2021-2022).

questions.stem: The CBIC recently held an outreach programme on GST 2.0 reforms. With reference to the institutional architecture of GST in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
GST Council decisions are taken by a simple majority of members present and voting, with each member having one vote.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct; CBIC is an attached body of the Department of Revenue administering indirect taxes. Statement 2 is incorrect because the GST Council, under Article 279A, decides by weighted voting (Centre has one-third weightage, states together two-thirds) and requires at least three-fourths of the weighted votes cast.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: CBIC holds outreach programme in Chandigarh to discuss GST 2.0 reforms with taxpayers
questions.pyqLink: Tests GST Council voting mechanism under Article 279A; similar to UPSC 2017 prelims question on GST Council composition and voting.

questions.stem: India and Mexico have launched negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA). With reference to types of trade agreements, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) involves tariff reduction or elimination on a limited list of goods, unlike a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) which generally covers a much wider range of goods and often services.
India is a member of the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA), which creates a preferential trading arrangement among SAARC member states.
A Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) is narrower in scope than a PTA since it excludes trade in services and investment.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct descriptions of PTA/FTA distinction and India's SAFTA membership. Statement 3 is wrong because a CECA is broader than a PTA, typically covering trade in goods, services, investment and other areas of economic cooperation, not narrower.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Mint Explainer | What does the proposed India-Mexico preferential trade agreement mean for Indian exporters?
questions.pyqLink: Tests the hierarchy of trade agreements (PTA/FTA/CECA/CEPA); similar in spirit to UPSC 2019 question on RCEP and trade agreement terminology.

questions.stem: The government has formed a high-level banking panel, while a drug regulator recently acted against Sun Pharma. Consider the following pairs of institutions and their descriptions:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO)
Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and regulates the quality of pharmaceutical exports
Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)
A statutory body established under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003, to oversee vigilance administration in the Union Government
Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
A body corporate established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, responsible for monetary policy and currency issuance
World Bank
An international financial institution, functioning as a specialized agency of the United Nations system, that publishes periodic country poverty and equity briefs
questions.explanation: Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are correctly matched. Pair 1 is incorrect because CDSCO functions under the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and regulates drugs, cosmetics and medical devices under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 — not under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Govt sets up high-level banking panel under Suresh N. Patel
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory/institutional affiliation of regulatory bodies; similar to UPSC pattern of matching regulators with their parent ministries/Acts (e.g., UPSC 2022 statutory bodies question).

questions.stem: At the Qiskit Fall Fest, experts highlighted quantum computing's potential in solving complex problems. With reference to quantum computing, which one of the following best describes its core computational advantage over classical computing?
options: It uses qubits that can exist in superposition and exploit entanglement, enabling certain computations to be performed far more efficiently than with classical bits for specific problem classes
It replaces silicon transistors with carbon nanotubes to increase clock speed while retaining the same binary logic gates as classical computers
It relies on parallel processing across multiple classical processors connected through a high-speed network to divide computational tasks
It uses DNA molecules to store and process information through biochemical reactions instead of electronic circuits
questions.explanation: Quantum computing's defining feature is the use of qubits that leverage superposition and entanglement, allowing certain classes of problems (e.g., factorization, optimization, simulation) to be solved far more efficiently than classical computers. Options B, C and D describe unrelated technologies (nanotechnology, classical distributed computing, and DNA computing respectively).
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Quantum tech can help solve complex problems: Jnan Yalla
questions.pyqLink: Tests basic conceptual understanding of quantum computing; similar to UPSC 2022/2023 prelims questions on emerging technologies like quantum computing and blockchain.

questions.stem: The Chief Economic Adviser recently compared India's present economic situation to 1991. In this context, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Chief Economic Adviser compared the current economic juncture to 1991, citing geopolitical tensions and import dependence on critical technologies as key vulnerabilities.

Statement-II: In 1991, India faced a severe balance of payments crisis due to depleting foreign exchange reserves, which forced it to undertake structural economic reforms including liberalization of trade and industrial policy.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct — the 1991 crisis and reforms are well-documented, and the CEA did draw the 1991 comparison over tech/geopolitical vulnerability. However, Statement-II does not explain Statement-I, since the CEA explicitly clarified that the comparison was not a prediction of another balance-of-payments crisis but referred to a broader structural inflection point in manufacturing, energy, agriculture and technology.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: '2026 resembles 1991': Why CEA V Anantha Nageswaran wants India to rethink its growth strategy — what he said
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of the 1991 BoP crisis and reforms alongside careful reading of current policy commentary; mirrors the Statement-I/Statement-II format introduced from UPSC 2022 onward.

questions.stem: With reference to India's Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), recently strengthened by the launch of NVS-03, which one of the following best describes the system?
options: It is a global positioning system with worldwide coverage similar to GPS, maintained by ISRO with a constellation of over 24 satellites.
It is a regional satellite navigation system developed by ISRO to provide position, navigation and timing services over the Indian landmass and a region extending about 1,500 km beyond its borders.
It is a satellite-based augmentation system that corrects GPS signals for civil aviation over Indian airspace, operated jointly by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India.
It is a constellation of geostationary communication satellites used exclusively for disaster warning and relay of meteorological data.
questions.explanation: NavIC/IRNSS is explicitly a regional system covering India and roughly 1,500 km beyond its geopolitical boundary, as the article notes. Option A wrongly describes it as a global system like GPS (which does use ~24+ satellites). Option C describes GAGAN, India's separate satellite-based augmentation system for aviation. Option D describes INSAT-type communication/meteorological satellites, a different ISRO programme.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: NVS-03 launched successfully; satellite placed in intended orbit | Highlights
questions.pyqLink: Tests GNSS types (GPS/GLONASS/Galileo/BeiDou vs regional NavIC/QZSS) and SBAS (GAGAN) — cf. UPSC 2019 question on GAGAN's purpose.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding cardamom cultivation and trade in India, in the context of recent payment delays to Kerala's cardamom exporters:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Cardamom is cultivated mainly in the Western Ghats region, principally in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
The Spices Board of India, which licenses cardamom auctioneers, functions under the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Cardamom auctions in India are conducted through e-auction platforms licensed by the Spices Board.
India is currently the world's largest exporter of cardamom by volume.
questions.explanation: Statements 1-3 are correct: cardamom is grown chiefly in the Western Ghats states, the Spices Board (under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry) licenses auctioneers, and e-auctions are the standard trading mechanism. Statement 4 is false — India is the largest producer of small cardamom but Guatemala has overtaken it as the world's largest exporter by volume, which is why Indian exporters face stiff competitive and payment-cycle pressures.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: West Asia crisis triggers payment concern in Keralam’s cardamom sector
questions.pyqLink: Tests commodity board institutional framework and India's trade ranking in plantation crops — a recurring PYQ theme on commodity boards under the Ministry of Commerce.

questions.stem: In the context of the reintroduction of cheetahs at Kuno National Park, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Kuno National Park, where African cheetahs have been reintroduced under Project Cheetah, is located in Madhya Pradesh.
The cheetahs introduced under Project Cheetah belong to the African subspecies, since the Asiatic cheetah now survives only in Iran.
The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is listed in Appendix II of CITES, which permits regulated international commercial trade in the species.
questions.explanation: Kuno National Park is in Madhya Pradesh, and since the Asiatic cheetah is extinct in India and survives only in Iran, the reintroduced cheetahs are of African origin — both statements are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the cheetah is listed in CITES Appendix I (barring a few southern African range states with quota exceptions), which prohibits rather than permits general international commercial trade.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Two held over death of cheetah; firearm as yet untraced
questions.pyqLink: Tests CITES appendices and Project Cheetah geography — similar to UPSC questions on CITES listing status of Indian wildlife species.

questions.stem:
In the context of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the controversy over alleged misuse of Form 7, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Election Commission of India derives its power to revise and update electoral rolls, including conducting a Special Intensive Revision, from Article 324 of the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Statement-II: Deletion of a voter's name from the electoral roll on an objection under Form 7 requires field verification and a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the elector concerned, under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: ECI's superintendence over elections flows from Article 324, while the preparation and revision of electoral rolls is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Statement-II is also correct: the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 mandate verification and a hearing before a name is deleted on objection. However, Statement-II describes a procedural safeguard in roll revision, not the source of ECI's constitutional/statutory power, so it does not explain Statement-I.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi denies defending SIR
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 324, Representation of the People Act 1950, and electoral roll revision procedure — recurring polity theme since the 2023-24 SIR controversies.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the geography of the cheetah reintroduction sites in Madhya Pradesh:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Kuno National Park lies in Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh, within the Aravalli hill range.
The Kuno River, a tributary of the Chambal River, flows through the park.
Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary, identified as a second site for cheetah reintroduction, is also located in Madhya Pradesh.
Kuno National Park falls within the Semi-Arid biogeographic zone of India as per the Rodgers and Panwar classification.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the Kuno River drains into the Chambal, and Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary (Mandsaur-Neemuch) in Madhya Pradesh is the designated second cheetah site. Statement 1 is wrong — Kuno lies within the Vindhyan hill system, not the Aravallis, which lie further northwest. Statement 4 is wrong — Kuno falls under the Deccan Peninsula biogeographic zone (Central Highlands province), not the Semi-Arid zone, which covers parts of Rajasthan and Gujarat.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Two held over death of cheetah; firearm as yet untraced
questions.pyqLink: Tests river systems (Chambal tributaries) and India's biogeographic classification — a recurring theme in physical/biogeography PYQs.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of entities associated with international cybersecurity and sanctions against North Korea's weapons programmes:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: TraderTraitor
North Korea-linked hacking group accused of the record cryptocurrency theft from the Binance exchange
FATF
Inter-governmental body that maintains 'grey' and 'black' lists of countries with inadequate anti-money-laundering controls
UNSC 1718 Committee
UN Security Council body overseeing sanctions imposed on North Korea over its nuclear and missile programmes
APT38
An Iran-based cyber-espionage group focused on disrupting critical infrastructure in Gulf countries
questions.explanation: TraderTraitor, FATF and the UNSC 1718 Committee are correctly matched: the first is the North Korean group linked to the Binance theft, FATF maintains the grey/black AML lists, and the 1718 Committee administers UN sanctions on North Korea. APT38 is mismatched — it is a North Korean (not Iranian) financially-motivated hacking unit, from whose ranks groups like TraderTraitor are said to have drawn operators, as noted in the article.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: North Korean hackers linked to crypto thefts among world's best, experts say
questions.pyqLink: Tests international sanctions architecture (UNSC sanctions committees, FATF) — static IR/institutions theme often tested via current cyber/sanctions news.

questions.stem:
With reference to India's institutional response to cybersecurity incidents such as cryptocurrency thefts by state-sponsored hacking groups, consider the following statements:
1. CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and is the national nodal agency for responding to cybersecurity incidents.
2. CERT-In derives its statutory mandate from the Information Technology Act, 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. CERT-In operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology as India's nodal cybersecurity incident response agency, and its constitution and functions are statutorily backed by Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: North Korean hackers linked to crypto thefts among world's best, experts say
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional/statutory basis of India's cybersecurity framework (CERT-In, IT Act 2000) — a recurring S&T-governance PYQ theme.

questions.stem: With reference to Legislative Councils in Indian states, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 169 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to create or abolish a Legislative Council in a State, based on a resolution passed by the State Legislative Assembly by special majority.
At present, Legislative Councils exist in six States: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
Members of a Legislative Council are directly elected by all adult citizens of the State in the same manner as members of the Legislative Assembly.
questions.explanation: Article 169 lets Parliament create/abolish a State Legislative Council on a special-majority resolution of the State Assembly, and India currently has six states with a Council. Statement 3 is wrong — MLCs are elected indirectly through an electoral college (MLAs, local bodies, and teachers'/graduates' constituencies) plus some nominated by the Governor, not by universal adult suffrage.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Legislative Council polls: How the intricate system to elect MLCs works
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 169 and bicameral state legislatures; similar to UPSC's recurring questions on Rajya Sabha/Vidhan Parishad composition and indirect election.

questions.stem: With reference to stock markets, which one of the following best describes the term 'market capitalisation' of a listed company?
options: The total value of a company's outstanding shares, calculated by multiplying the current market price per share by the total number of outstanding shares
The total revenue earned by a company during a financial year as reported in its audited annual accounts
The net worth of a company arrived at by subtracting total liabilities from total assets as shown in its balance sheet
The total amount of capital raised by a company through its initial public offering on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Market capitalisation is the stock market's valuation of a company, computed as share price multiplied by total outstanding shares — the figure cited for Trent Ltd (Rs 1.63 lakh crore). Revenue, net worth, and IPO proceeds are distinct accounting/corporate-finance concepts, not market capitalisation.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Who is Bahram Vakil, the corporate lawyer set to succeed Noel Tata at Trent?
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static finance term 'market capitalisation', in the flagship UPSC 'best describes the term' format (cf. Merchant Discount Rate, 2019).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding cryptocurrency and blockchain technology:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: A cryptocurrency private key is a cryptographic code that allows its holder to access and transfer the digital assets associated with a specific wallet address.
A blockchain is a centralised ledger maintained by a single regulatory authority that records all cryptocurrency transactions.
'Proof of Reserves' refers to an independent verification that a cryptocurrency exchange holds sufficient assets to cover all customer deposits.
In India, income from the transfer of Virtual Digital Assets is currently exempt from taxation under the Income Tax Act.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: private keys control wallet access, and Proof of Reserves verifies an exchange's solvency. Statement 2 is wrong — a blockchain is a decentralised, distributed ledger, not centrally controlled. Statement 4 is wrong — Virtual Digital Asset transfer income is taxed at a flat 30% under Section 115BBH of the Income Tax Act.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Binance security breach: How 'biggest-ever' hack happened, its impact on Indian crypto market
questions.pyqLink: Tests blockchain/cryptocurrency fundamentals and India's VDA tax regime, a growing current-affairs-meets-static theme since 2022.

questions.stem: With reference to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A GLOF occurs due to the sudden release of water impounded by a glacier or a moraine dam.
The National Disaster Management Authority has attributed rising GLOF risk in the Himalayas partly to glacier retreat caused by climate change.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. A GLOF is the sudden release of water dammed by a glacier or a moraine (debris accumulation), and the NDMA links the growing frequency of such events to climate-change-driven glacier retreat in the Himalayas, as seen in the Bhutan-triggered alert affecting Assam and West Bengal.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Bhutan GLOF explained: What are glacial lake outburst floods, and why are such events recurring in Himalayas?
questions.pyqLink: Tests GLOF mechanics and NDMA's disaster-risk framework for the Himalayas, building on the 2023 Sikkim GLOF disaster.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs regarding Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's early political career:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Kheda Satyagraha (1918)
Movement seeking revenue relief for peasants in Gujarat hit by crop failure
Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)
Launched in the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
Gujarat Provincial Congress Committee
Formed after the 1920 Nagpur Congress session decided to set up provincial committees
Champaran Satyagraha
Patel's first mass movement as a Satyagrahi under Gandhi's leadership
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is incorrect — the Champaran Satyagraha (1917, Bihar, over indigo cultivation) was Gandhi's first movement in India but did not involve Patel; Patel's first mass movement as a Satyagrahi was the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: On Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary, a historian explains how he became 'Sardar'
questions.pyqLink: Tests sequencing and ownership of early Gandhian movements (Champaran, Kheda, Non-Cooperation), a recurring PYQ theme on freedom movement chronology.

questions.stem: With reference to the Sankosh river, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Sankosh river originates in Bhutan and eventually joins the Brahmaputra river in Assam.
The Sankosh is a major tributary of the Teesta river in North Bengal.
questions.explanation: The Sankosh rises in the Bhutan Himalayas, flows through Bhutan into Assam and West Bengal, and joins the Brahmaputra — consistent with the GLOF-triggered flood alerts in Kokrajhar, Dhubri, and Cooch Behar along its banks. It is not a tributary of the Teesta, which is a separate Himalayan river system in North Bengal/Sikkim.

questions.sourceTitle: Bhutan GLOF explained: What are glacial lake outburst floods, and why are such events recurring in Himalayas?
questions.pyqLink: Tests Himalayan river drainage systems and tributaries of the Brahmaputra, a recurring Geography PYQ theme.
